analysis.one_liner: Tech Mahindra is a Mahindra Group IT services and BPO company that runs telecom, manufacturing, BFSI and other enterprise clients' technology and network operations.
analysis.whats_happening: Tech Mahindra reported Q2 FY27 (September quarter) results on 15 October 2026: revenue/total income of about ₹16,173 crore, up ~15% YoY and 3% QoQ, and net profit of roughly ₹1,586-1,610 crore (exact figure varies slightly by source), up ~33% YoY and 8.2% QoQ. The board declared an interim dividend of ₹15/share and recommended a 1:1 bonus share issue; record date is not yet announced. The stock jumped and is now at its 52-week/all-time high of ₹1,790.
analysis.plain_terms: This is an IT-services company that builds and runs technology for telecom operators and other large businesses. The latest quarter looked strong, but a good chunk of the profit jump came from internal cost-cutting (an efficiency push called 'Project Fortius'), not purely from winning more business - so the quality of the growth matters as much as its size. The company is also handing out bonus shares, which just splits the same ownership into more shares and does not by itself make anyone richer. The tension: the stock is already at an all-time high and priced well above peers, so the market has largely given credit for this turnaround in advance.
analysis.quarters: Profit momentum has been uneven: Q2 FY26 (year-ago quarter) PAT had actually fallen 4.4% YoY to ₹1,194.5 crore, which makes this quarter's 32-34% YoY profit jump look better partly because of that soft base. The more telling number is the sequential (QoQ) move: profit up 8.2% and revenue up 3% QoQ, which is a cleaner read on current momentum. EBIT margin rose to 14.8%, management's twelfth consecutive quarter of margin expansion, driven by Project Fortius cost actions (lower subcontracting, more fixed-price work, better offshore utilisation) plus genuine volume growth - new deal wins of $1,023 million, up 25.4% YoY, the fourth straight quarter above $1 billion in bookings.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is at an all-time high with 0% drawdown from peak, so there is no crash to explain here. Returns have been strongly ahead of both the Nifty and peer HCLTECH over 1 year (+26.8% vs Nifty -9.5%, peer -3.9%) and 3 years (+63.9% vs Nifty +16.8%, peer +22.7%), but over 5 years the stock (+44.0%) is roughly in line with the peer (+40.2%) and only modestly ahead of the Nifty (+25.3%). That pattern suggests most of the outperformance is a recent turnaround story (last 1-3 years) following a weaker 2021-2023 stretch, not a steady multi-year compounder. The only corporate action on record is a 2015 2:1 split, which is not relevant to any price fall since there has been none recently.
analysis.valuation_read: Trailing P/E is reported in a range of roughly 27x-31x and P/B around 4.95x-5.45x depending on the data source and exact date, both sitting at roughly a 25-45% premium to peer medians. Why it looks expensive: the market is paying up for the Project Fortius margin story, which has actually been delivered for 12 straight quarters. Whether it is cheap - no, by both P/E and P/B it screens expensive against IT-services peers, meaning a lot of the expected margin delivery is already priced in; further re-rating likely needs the 15% FY27 margin target to be reached and sustained, or revenue growth to re-accelerate, not just the current trend continuing.
analysis.growth_read: Revenue grew ~15% YoY / 3% QoQ on real new business (deal wins of $1,023 million, up 25.4% YoY) - this is volume-led, not just price increases. But profit grew roughly twice as fast as revenue, so a significant part of the quarter's growth is margin-led, coming from cost actions under Project Fortius rather than pure volume expansion. That margin tailwind is time-limited: once the FY27 15% EBIT margin target is reached, growth will need to come mainly from revenue again.
analysis.health_read: Debt-to-equity is reported as negligible/near zero, so financial (balance-sheet) risk is low. ROE of roughly 17-19.5% and ROCE of about 23% are both well above sector medians cited by multiple sources (~10.6% and ~12.9% respectively), indicating decent capital efficiency. Whether profits are converting cleanly into operating cash flow was not independently verified in this search - check the cash flow statement on Screener. The bigger risk here looks like business risk (client/vertical concentration in telecom, pricing pressure, execution on the margin target) rather than financial risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (Mahindra Group entities: Mahindra & Mahindra 25.31%, TML Benefit Trust 9.62%, Mahindra-BT Mauritius 0.02%) hold about 34.97% of the company, roughly unchanged recently, with zero shares pledged - a clean promoter position. Domestic institutions (DIIs) hold about 36.9%, slightly more than the promoter stake, while foreign institutions (FIIs) hold about 18.7% - domestic funds have a noticeably larger bet here than foreign investors. No globally recognised individual marquee investor was found on the shareholder register in the sources checked; if you were expecting one, they are not there.
strengths: EBIT margin has expanded for 12 consecutive quarters to 14.8%, up ~260 bps YoY, closing in on the FY27 Project Fortius target of 15%.
Zero promoter pledge and near-zero debt-to-equity - a clean, low-financial-risk balance sheet.
New deal wins of $1,023 million in the quarter (up 25.4% YoY), the fourth straight quarter above $1 billion in bookings - order momentum looks real, not just cost-cutting optics.
ROE (~17-19.5%) and ROCE (~23%) both sit well above the sector medians cited (~10.6% and ~12.9%).
watchpoints: Valuation is already rich: P/E ~27-31x and P/B ~4.95-5.45x represent a 25-45% premium to peer medians, at an all-time high with zero drawdown - little room for a disappointing quarter.

A meaningful part of this quarter's 32-34% YoY profit growth is flattered by a weak year-ago base (Q2 FY26 PAT had fallen 4.4% YoY) - the smaller 8.2% QoQ profit gain is the more honest momentum signal.

Margin gains have leaned heavily on cost actions (subcontracting cuts, fixed-price mix, offshore efficiency) rather than pricing power; once the 15% target is reached, the easy margin gains run out and growth has to come from revenue.
The 1:1 bonus issue is cosmetic - it increases share count and proportionally lowers the price without changing company value; it should not be read as a fundamental catalyst.
analysis.one_thing: Whether EBIT margin actually crosses and holds at the 15% Project Fortius target over the next two quarters - that will show whether the current premium valuation is earned by delivery or is running ahead of it.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q2 FY27 results across Business Standard, TradingView/Moody's, Kotak Neo, mid-east.info and Upstox; sources showed a minor discrepancy in the exact PAT figure (₹1,585.6 crore vs ₹1,609.7 crore) and in P/E (26.35x to 31.3x depending on provider and exact date) - both ranges are reported here rather than averaged. Promoter holding (34.97%, zero pledge) and FII/DII splits (18.66% / ~36.9%) were consistent across sources checked. Operating-cash-flow conversion of profit and the exact bonus-issue record date were not verified - check on Screener/NSE filings.
